sentences.text: CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANANT RAMANATH HEGDE  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANANT RAMANATH HEGDE) Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants and the learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents/State.
2. Since common question is involved in all these appeals, with the consent of counsel on both sides the appeals are heard together.
The question involved in this case is about the market value of the lands acquired.

4. The claimants are seeking enhancement of compensation challenging the judgments and awards in LACs Nos.155/2009, 153/2009, 157/2009, 154/2009, 159/2009, 152/2009 and 156/2009 respectively on the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Chincholi and the judgment and award in LACAs No.440/2019, 206/2016, 181/2015, 439/2019, 207/2016, 220/2016, 180/2015 on the file of the IV Additional District Judge, Kalaburagi Sitting at Sedam, III Additional District Judge, Kalaburagi and IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi respectively.
5.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the said awards, the respective claimants have filed reference petitions as specified in column No.4 of the tabular chart.
9. The Reference Court enhanced the market value to Rs.1,92,000/- per acre in all cases.
Later, the respective claimants aggrieved by the award passed by the Reference Court have filed appeals before the First Appellate Court as specified in column No.3 of the chart.
11. The First Appellate Court enhanced the market value to Rs.5,10,000/- per acre in all cases except LACA No.181/2015 and LACA No.180/2015.
In both these appeals, the Appellate Court awarded Rs.4,48,200/- per acre as the market value.
12. Both the Courts have given a finding that the lands acquired were irrigated lands.
Even the Land Acquisition Officer had treated the acquired lands as irrigated lands.
13. The appellants are before this Court seeking further enhancement.
14. It is also relevant to note that the State has accepted the award passed by the First Appellate Court.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants would submit that the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Miscellaneous Second Appeal No.200064/2020 has determined the market value at a sum of Rs.6,17,168/- per acre in respect of land bearing Sy.No.82/2C of Tumkunta village,
Chincholi Taluka.
The land involved in the said proceeding was acquired in terms of notification dated 05.04.2007.
Admittedly, the land involved in the said proceedings were dry land.

16. Learned counsel for the appellants have also placed reliance on the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.200196/2014, where in respect of the land acquired in terms of the notification dated 05.04.2007, the Division Bench of this Court has awarded compensation of Rs.6,17,168/- per acre.

It is noticed that in the said case, the property acquired was Sy.No.36/2A/12B measuring 11 acres 1 gunta of - 18 - Pandu S/O Chandunayak And Ors vs The Chief Engineer And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56712840/

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the said land was dry land.

17. Learned counsel for the claimants would submit that the lands involved in these cases being the irrigated lands one and half times the market value of dry lands is to be awarded and prays to award Rs.9,25,752/- per acre.

18. Learned Additional Advocate General for the respondent/State would oppose the prayer of the appellants and submits that the market value is determined by the First Appellate Court having due regard to the evidence placed before it and prays for dismissal of the appeals.

19. After considering the contentions raised and on perusal of the records, this Court is of the view that the following point arises for consideration:
- 19 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6970 MSA NO. 200263 of 2021 MSA NO.200264 of 2021 MSA NO. 200265 of 2021 MSA NO. 200272 of 2021 "Whether the claimants/appellants have made out a case for awarding compensation by fixing market value at Rs.9,25,752/-?"
20.

It is relevant to note that the appellants are placing reliance on the judgment of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court and the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court referred to supra to justify their claim for higher compensation.
At the outset, it is to be noticed in the judgments relied on by the learned counsel for the appellants, the lands involved were of Tumkunta village, Taluka Chincholi.
In the instant case, the lands are located in Shadipur village, Taluka Chincholi.
21. The Google map would reveal that the distance between Shadipur village and Tumkunta village is 22 Kms.

Prima facie, the market value determined in MFA No.200196/2014 in respect of land located in Tumkunta - 20 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6970 MSA NO. 200263 of 2021 MSA NO.200264 of 2021 MSA NO. 200265 of 2021 MSA NO. 200272 of 2021 village cannot be applied to determine the market value of the land located in Shadipur village, Taluka Chincholi.

22. In a similar situation, in Miscellaneous Second Appeal No.200112/2016, where the Court was called upon to apply the market value determined in another village of the same Taluka, this Court had secured the guidance value of the properties in Chincholi Taluka for the relevant period.

Learned Additional Advocate General had furnished the guidance value maintained by the jurisdictional Sub- Registrar in respect of lands in Chincholi Taluka from 01.08.2002 to 30.11.2007 and in addition, the revised guidance value for the period from 01.12.2007 to 31.05.2009 is also Pandu S/O Chandunayak And Ors vs The Chief Engineer And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56712840/

sentences.text: The chart below would disclose the guidance value of the lands in Shadipur and Tumkunta village, Taluka Chincholi.

- 21 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6970 MSA NO. 200263 of 2021 MSA NO.200264 of 2021 MSA NO. 200265 of 2021 MSA NO. 200272 of 2021 Shadipur (period from 01.08.2002 to 30.11.2007) Black cotton Masaari Maradi Tari Rs.28,910/- Rs.23,650/- Rs.21,020/- Rs.43,560/-
Shadipur (period from 01.12.2007 to 31.5.2009) Black cotton Masaari Maradi Tari Rs.34,000/-
Rs.28,000/- Rs.24,000/- Rs.55,000/-
Tumkunta (period from 01.08.2002 to 31.11.2007) Black cotton Masaari Maradi Tari Rs.38,720/-
Rs.31,680/- Rs.28,160/- Rs.59,950/-
24.

As could be seen from the said guidance value register maintained by the Sub-Registrar, the market value of black cotton soil land in Shadipur village is Rs.28,910/- per acre, Rs.23,650/- per acre is for Masaari land and Rs.21,020/- per acre is for Maradi land.
It is also noticed that it is Rs.43,560/- per acre for Tari (irrigated) land.

In the same register, the valuation of the property in Tumkunta village, Taluka Chincholi is also given, wherein, the valuation of the land having black soil is Rs.38,720/-
- 22 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6970 MSA NO. 200263 of 2021 MSA NO.200264 of 2021 MSA NO. 200265 of 2021 MSA NO. 200272 of 2021 per acre, Rs.31,680/- per acre is for Masaari land, Rs.28,160/- per acre is for Maradi land and for Tari (irrigated) land, it is Rs.59,950/- per acre.
25.

It is also noticed that the guidance value of black cotton soil land in Shadipur village for the period from 01.12.2007 to 31.05.2009 is fixed at Rs.34,000/- per acre, for Masaari land, it is Rs.28,000/- per acre, for Maradi land, it is Rs.24,000/- per acre and for irrigated land, it is Rs.55,000/- per acre.

Likewise, for Tumkunta village, the guidance value for the period covering 01.08.2002 to 31.11.2007, for black cotton soil is Rs.38,720/- per acre, Rs.31,680/- per acre is for Masaari land, Rs.28,160/- per acre is for Maradi land and Rs.59,950/- per acre is for irrigated land.

26. As can be noticed from the aforementioned figures, the value of the land in Tumkunta village was always more than the value of the land in Shadipur village.
- 23 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6970 MSA NO. 200263 of 2021 MSA NO.200264 of 2021 MSA NO. 200265 of 2021 MSA NO. 200272 of 2021 For the relevant period i.e., from 01.08.2002 to 30.11.2007, if the Pandu S/O Chandunayak And Ors vs The Chief Engineer And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56712840/
15 value of lands in both villages is compared, the valuation of the land in Shadipur village is 25.44/%
less than the valuation in Tumkunta village. Thus, it is apparent that the valuation in Shadipur is less than in Tumkunta.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of the view that the valuation of the land in Tumkunta village determined by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court cannot straight away be applied to determine the market value of the land in Shadipur village.

There has to be proportionate deduction in the value and by deducting 25.44% from the value determined by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, in respect of land located in Tumkunta village, the valuation of the land in Shadipur village would come to Rs.4,60,160/-.

Since the valuation determined by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in respect of the land in Tumkunta village is in respect of dry land,
this figure of - 24 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6970 MSA NO. 200263 of 2021 MSA NO.200264 of 2021 MSA NO. 200265 of 2021 MSA NO. 200272 of 2021 Rs.4,60,160/- would be the value in respect of dry land in Shadipur village.
27. Admittedly, the lands acquired in this case are irrigated lands.
This is the finding given by the Special Land Acquisition Officer in his award and the same is confirmed by the Reference Court and the First Appellate Court.
The State has not questioned the said finding.
It is stated by the learned Additional Advocate General that the valuation of the irrigated land would be 1 times of the value of the dry land.

Applying the said formula, the valuation would come to Rs.6,90,240/- per acre.
28.
For the reasons recorded above, the contentions of the appellants that the appellants are entitled to a market value of Rs.9,25,752/- is to be rejected.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i.
The appeals are allowed with cost.
The appellants in all the appeals are entitled to the market value of Rs.6,90,240/- per acre with all statutory benefits.
